today_take.headline: AI 활용의 과제가 예측값을 만드는 데서 실제 의사결정과 업무 완료까지 연결하는 데로 옮겨가고 있다.
today_take.body: 무신사는 예측을 넘어 결정과 발견을 지원하려고 DeciML과 NeXA를 만들었고, 컬리는 기획서에서 결함 등록까지 이어지는 QA AI Hub를 다뤘다. 두 사례에서 공통으로 드러나는 관심은 모델의 출력 자체보다 그 출력으로 다음 업무까지 수행하는 것이다. 네이버의 Multi-interest 개발이 ‘딸깍’으로 되지 않았다는 문제의식도, 이런 연결이 단순한 도구 도입만으로 끝나지 않는다는 흐름과 맞닿아 있다.

hn.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
hn.content: 日本語 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights Authors Rikiya Takehi * Jayden Teoh * Alex Zhang Omar Khattab Affiliations MIT CSAIL MIT CSAIL MIT CSAIL MIT CSAIL Published November 2, 2026 TL;DR We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights , using a variety of recent tools and algorithms or even via direct weight editing. These results show sparks of Weight-Space Programming, which may extend beyond what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. This might be a big deal for both optimization and interpretability. Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights . With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x. All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming . Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon. This is changing: our neural network weights will soon be natively optimized by LLMs that deliberately reason about their weights . Read Which game was this neural network trained on? Astra reads the 17,253 weights, with no tools Breakout 99% confident Fix A trained policy never gets the car over the strip. Astra ed
hn.summary:
LLM이 신경망 가중치를 직접 읽고 수정하는 ‘Weight-Space Programming’의 가능성을 보여주는 연구다.
- GPT-6 Astra는 원시 가중치만 보고 신경망이 어떤 작업을 수행하도록 학습됐는지 식별했다.
- 환경 피드백 없이 처음부터 작은 게임용 신경망을 작성해, PPO로 1억 스텝 학습한 신경망보다 높은 성능을 냈다.
- 학습 루프나 그래디언트 없이 Qwen3.5-0.8B의 추론 반복 문제를 찾아 가중치의 0.016%를 직접 수정했다. 동일한 샘플링 설정에서 MATH-500 점수는 7.9%에서 48.1%로, IFEval 점수는 3배로 높아졌다.

hn.title: WTF Ubuntu?
hn.content: WTF Ubuntu? 2026-11-02 What the fuck, Ubuntu? In case you missed it: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) bug in the Linux kernel's TCP code. It's been there since 2016, so virtually every Linux server on the planet has it, and it can be hit remotely. Anthropic says it built a working exploit that gets root on a server. A total takeover. Debian patched it on October 16 . Ubuntu still doesn't have a patch more than two weeks later. Every supported release, LTS included, is listed as "Vulnerable". Ubuntu's website promises "timely patches for critical vulnerabilities." Ubuntu hasn't shipped the patch nine days after it was rated 9.8 and six days after a working root exploit. Very fucking timely indeed. Software is full of this blabber where words mean nothing. Ubuntu uses words like these: "Timely." "Enterprise-grade." "Production grade." "Enterprise resilience. Developer velocity. Build with confidence on Ubuntu." Somebody, or perhaps worse, some special team at Canonical is dedicated to writing these........ So I'm asking again... What the fuck, Ubuntu? I'm moving all my servers off Ubuntu. I've completely lost trust in it. On the desktop I always hated it anyway. On servers I mostly used it because it's the default on most VPS providers, and I considered it the solid, no-drama LTS distro. Fuck that now. I can't express how crazy this is. I didn't have time to migrate my services and data when I learned about this, so I had to take all my servers that run Ubuntu offline. Oh and btw, distros run by volunteers (Debian, Arch, Alpine...) hve shipped the fix. Meanwhile Ubuntu, made by a company that sells security subscriptions, hasn't. This is true as of 2026-11-02 14:48 UTC. Added after this blew up: Can't beat all the bullshit, so I parody it at Bloatberg .
hn.summary:
치명적인 Linux 커널 취약점에 대한 Ubuntu의 패치 지연을 비판하며 서버 이전을 선언한 글이다.
- 글에 따르면 CVE-2026-98432는 2016년부터 존재한 Linux 커널 TCP 코드의 원격 공격 취약점으로, CVSS 9.8이며 Anthropic은 서버의 root 권한을 획득하는 익스플로잇을 만들었다고 밝혔다.
- Debian은 10월 16일 패치했지만, 11월 2일 작성된 이 글은 Ubuntu의 모든 지원 버전이 LTS를 포함해 여전히 취약한 상태라고 지적한다.
- 저자는 신속한 패치를 약속한 Ubuntu에 신뢰를 잃었다며 모든 서버를 다른 배포판으로 이전하겠다고 선언했고, 즉시 이전할 시간이 없어 Ubuntu 서버를 모두 오프라인으로 전환했다고 밝혔다.

hn.title: If you love a website, back it up
hn.content: This story starts with a little tragedy. See, I’ve got these old webpages I love to go back and look on every now and then. There’s websites that have been online unchanged for years and years, or decades, and there’s something a little cozy about checking in on them every now and then to see an old friend is still doing okay. Sometimes, of course, tragedy strikes. There was this fansite called teapuppies.com for an old anime series and and toy line called Ochaken . It’s about these cute cartoon dog characters who have tea leaves for ears, each of them named after a different kind of tea. 1 The site had been online since 2004 and had basically not changed since 2005, but it was nice just having it around. Except when I went to visit it a few weeks ago, and discovered that not only was the site gone but the domain is now being used to serve online gambling ads. I work in web archiving, by the way. Which is to say that I should have known the site would go offline someday, and that I have the tools to have done something about it. I could have archived that site while it was still around, but I didn’t. This post is here to beg you to do what I didn’t think to, and to teach you how. You see, when I talk to a lot of people about web archiving, they always seem to believe it’s something they couldn’t do. It’s something a big organization like the Internet Archive does, and if you want a webpage to be saved you just have to wait and hope it gets done. But that’s not true! What I really want everyone to know is that you have control over the world around you, you can take action to preserve things and make things better. And not just can , but should ! Don’t just wait for someone else to act - get out there and and make it happen! Got a favourite site? Back it up! Got some information you don’t want to get lost? Back it up! Favourite post somewhere? All together now. Back! It! Up! All of the tools I’ll be showing off in this post use standard web archiving formats like WAR
hn.summary:
오래된 팬사이트가 사라진 경험을 통해 개인도 웹사이트 보존에 나서야 한다고 촉구하는 글.
- Ochaken 팬사이트 teapuppies.com은 2004년부터 운영됐으며, 2005년 이후 거의 바뀌지 않은 상태로 남아 있었다.
- 저자가 몇 주 전 다시 방문했을 때 사이트는 사라졌고, 도메인은 온라인 도박 광고에 사용되고 있었다.
- 웹 아카이빙 분야에서 일하는 저자는 도구가 있었는데도 사이트를 보존하지 않은 일을 후회하며, 웹 보존은 Internet Archive 같은 대형 기관만 할 수 있는 일이 아니라고 강조한다.
